figures_added.what: Number line from -3 to 7 for 'How many integers satisfy -2 <= x < 6?'. Closed circle at -2 (<= included), open circle at 6 (< excluded), highlighted segment between. Theme-safe (currentColor axis/text, soft-blue segment with opacity). Exam convention: open/closed circles mark inclusion, exactly what a GCSE paper prints for an integer-range question.
Number line from 0 to 9 for 'How many integers satisfy 1 < x < 8?'. Open circles at both 1 and 8 (both strict), highlighted segment between. Endpoints match the display exactly.

notes: Inequalities is a largely textual unit. Figures were added only to the two problems whose display gives an explicit integer x-range (bronze[3], bronze[6]) - precisely where an exam prints a number line and where the figure can match the numbers without first solving. The solve/count problems (e.g. x^2<16, three-part inequalities) show their range only after algebra, so a number line of the unsolved statement would mislead; deliberately left figure-free. No question text, solution, guided step, hint or misconception was changed in this pass. Both SVGs: viewBox + role=img + aria-label, no external refs, <1KB each. Validator PASS; diagram checker cross-checked every circle type and endpoint against the display.
